findings.summary: NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo() are not gated by readOnly at the API surface; only the keybinding and toolbar button are conditionally omitted
findings.evidence: In packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts the returned API's undo/redo (lines 431-438) call runHistory('undo'/'redo') unconditionally, which calls store.undo()/redo() regardless of the readOnly flag passed to initialize(). Only the historyKeymap (Mod-z/Mod-Shift-z) is skipped when readOnly is true (buildExtensions), and the vim-command router additionally checks state.facet(EditorView.editable) before delegating to the store. Any caller that invokes api.undo()/api.redo() directly (devtools, a differently-wired UI surface, or a future toolbar that forgets the !readOnly gate seen in notes-toolbar.tsx line 200) can still push a Yorkie CRDT change from a client meant to be read-only. This mirrors the pre-existing pattern for toggleBold/insertTable (also unguarded at the API level), and notes-view.tsx documents that real write enforcement happens server-side ('the auth webhook would reject the update'), so this is defense-in-depth only rather than a demonstrated bypass. Flagging because it is a new call path (store-owned undo/redo) introduced by this diff.

findings.summary: Production code depends on a Document API explicitly named for test use (getUndoStackForTest), not a security-hardened contract
findings.evidence: YorkieNoteStore's constructor computes this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts, constructor) using doc.getUndoStackForTest(), an SDK helper whose name signals a test-only introspection API. The undo floor is the mechanism that stops a user from undoing the note's seeded content into an empty/contentless document; if this helper's semantics change or it is removed upstream (since it isn't a documented public contract), the floor could silently read 0 or throw, weakening the one guard that keeps undo from destroying the note's baseline content. Not an exploitable vulnerability today, but worth a security-relevant note since it underlies a data-integrity guard.

findings.summary: routeVimHistoryToStore(), which monkey-patches CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo to route vim's `u`/`<C-r>` keys to the store's history, has no test exercising it at all.
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:36-59 adds `routeVimHistoryToStore()` — a global monkeypatch of `CodeMirror.commands.undo`/`redo` that reads `noteStoreFacet` off `cm.cm6.state` and calls `store.undo()/redo()`, falling back to the original vim command otherwise. packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts only tests the CodeMirror keymap path ('binds Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z to the store history', lines 107-137) and the 'switches the keybinding mode (default <-> vim)' test (lines 156-172) only checks that switching to vim preserves text — it never presses `u` or `<C-r>` in vim mode to verify the routing actually fires or falls through correctly on a read-only mount. findings.summary: The new batch-folding branch of setLocalSelection (publishing presence through the batch's ambient root/presence instead of opening a nested doc.update) is never exercised by a test.
findings.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:171-196 adds an `if (this.activeRoot && this.activePresence)` branch so a selection publish made while a top-level batch() is open folds into the ambient update rather than opening a second `doc.update` (which the comment explicitly says would be 'an update inside an update'). No test in yorkie-note-store.test.ts or notes-undo-integration.test.ts calls `setLocalSelection` at all, let alone from inside a `batch()` callback, so this new reentrancy-avoidance path — precisely the kind of thing likely to throw or silently no-op if wrong — has no coverage.

findings.summary: The 'Mod-y' redo keybinding (distinct from the tested 'Mod-Shift-z' entry) is never pressed in a test.
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:220-236 registers three keymap entries, including a separate `{ key: 'Mod-y', mac: 'Mod-Shift-z', run: ... }` entry. The test at packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts:107-137 only presses Ctrl-Shift-Z, which matches the other 'Mod-Shift-z' entry, not 'Mod-y'. Low impact since both entries call the same `runHistory('redo')` closure, but the binding itself (e.g. a typo in the key string) would not be caught.

findings.summary: CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo is patched globally at module scope (once per process) rather than scoped to notes' own editor instances; it correctly re-resolves the NoteStore per call via the calling view's facet, so today's only consumer (notes vim mode) is unaffected, but any future non-notes code importing @replit/codemirror-vim or calling CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo directly would silently pick up notes' routing/fallback behavior instead of the original command.
findings.evidence: CodeMirror.commands.undo = route('undo'); CodeMirror.commands.redo = route('redo'); mutates the shared module-scoped CodeMirror.commands table exported by @replit/codemirror-vim.

findings.summary: Undo/redo can re-enter doc.update() through the peer-selection publish path while Yorkie is still dispatching the undo/redo change, risking a reentrancy failure in the SDK.
findings.evidence: doc.history.undo()/redo() (yorkie-note-store.ts:98,103) synchronously fires a local-change('undoredo') event, forwarded by subscribeRemote (yorkie-note-store.ts:130-168) to note-sync's applyRemote (note-sync.ts:25-52) via view.dispatch(). That same dispatch also runs NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update() (remote-selection.ts:109-121), which unconditionally calls store.setLocalSelection(...) on every ViewUpdate. Because the top-level batch() from the earlier forward edit has already closed by the time undo()/redo() is invoked, activeRoot is null, so setLocalSelection (yorkie-note-store.ts:171-194) takes the `this.doc.update(...)` branch, opening a second, nested doc.update() call on the same Document while doc.history.undo()/redo() is still on the call stack synchronously notifying subscribers. None of the added tests assert this selection-publish path doesn't throw or desync presence/undo state; if Document.update() is not reentrant-safe, every undo/redo could throw or corrupt state.

findings.summary: runHistory() reads view.state to recompute active formats immediately after calling store[kind](), assuming Yorkie's undo/redo event dispatch (and the CodeMirror transaction it triggers) is fully synchronous; if it is not, the toolbar briefly reflects stale (pre-undo) formats instead of the reverted document's formats.
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:205-208 — `store[kind](); selectionCb?.(computeActiveFormats(view.state));` with no confirmation that view.state has already absorbed the reverted transaction by this point.

findings.summary: Every docChanged ViewUpdate opens a store.batch() even when the loop over transactions ends up doing nothing (all transactions filtered out, e.g. a remote-tagged transaction). For YorkieNoteStore this still invokes doc.update() with an empty callback on every remote/peer-driven transaction, which is extra work and an extra (albeit presumably no-op) mutation call into the CRDT on every incoming remote edit and on every undo/redo echo.
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:61-77 wraps the whole transaction loop unconditionally in `this.store.batch(() => {...})`, with no early return when none of update.transactions will produce an editText call.

+# Notes native undo — lessons (issue #604)
+
+## Context
+
+Migrate WaffleNotes undo/redo from CodeMirror local history to Yorkie
+`doc.history`, so undo preserves peers' concurrent edits.
+
+## Lessons
+
+- The issue's prerequisite spike resolved cleanly: `Text.edit()` reverse
+  ops are supported on `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13. The `Tree.editByPath`
+  merge caveat that motivated the spike is a Tree-only limitation and
+  never applied to notes, whose whole content is one `Text`.
+- An empty `doc.update()` pushes nothing onto the undo stack, so
+  `batch()` does not need to pre-check whether the body will mutate.
+- Disabling `basicSetup`'s `history()` silently breaks vim's `u` /
+  `<C-r>` too: `@replit/codemirror-vim` routes them through
+  `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`, which call `@codemirror/commands`'
+  `undo(view)` and no-op without the history extension. The static
+  `CodeMirror.commands` map is read at call time, so overriding it is
+  the supported-shaped hook; its `:undo` ex-command copy is snapshotted
+  at module load and cannot be re-routed.
+- Undo granularity changes: CM history groups keystrokes by time
+  (`newGroupDelay`), Yorkie's unit is one change. One CM transaction =
+  one undo unit, so undo now steps per keystroke — the same behavior
+  Docs and Slides already have after their migrations.

+# Notes native undo — migrate to Yorkie `doc.history` (issue #604)
+
+PR: (to be filled after opening)
+
+## Goal
+
+Move WaffleNotes undo/redo off CodeMirror's local history onto
+Yorkie-native undo (`doc.history`), so undo carries CRDT semantics and
+preserves a peer's concurrent edits instead of last-write-wins-ing over
+them. Reuses the pattern already shipped in Slides
+(`docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md`) and Docs
+(`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`).
+
+## Prerequisite spike (done — result recorded here)
+
+Verified against the pinned `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13 that character-level
+`Text.edit()` **is** reversible through `doc.history`:
+
+- Two `content.edit()` calls inside ONE `doc.update()` push exactly one
+  undo-stack entry; `history.undo()` reverts both, `redo()` re-applies.
+- The undo emits a `local-change` event with `source === 'undoredo'`
+  carrying `edit` ops on `$.content` with correct `from`/`to`/`content`
+  (already reversed in apply order), i.e. the dormant `isUndoRedo` path
+  in `yorkie-note-store.ts` receives exactly what it needs.
+- A `doc.update()` whose body mutates nothing pushes **no** undo entry,
+  so an empty batch is free.
+
+(`Tree.editByPath` merge non-reversibility, called out in the issue,
+does not apply — notes store markdown in a single `Text`.)
+
+## Approach
+
+**Store layer (`packages/notes/src/store/store.ts`)** — extend
+`NoteStore` with `batch(fn)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`,
+`canRedo()`. Undo becomes store-owned (like `DocStore`/`SlidesStore`)
+rather than view-owned.
+
+**`YorkieNoteStore`** — ambient-root + `withUpdate()`: a top-level
+`batch()` opens ONE `doc.update()` and every `editText()` runs against
+that ambient root, so one CodeMirror transaction group = one Yorkie
+change = one undo unit. `setLocalSelection` folds into the batch's
+ambient presence proxy when a batch is open. `undo()/redo()` delegate to
+`doc.history`, gated by an undo floor captured at construction (after
+`ensureText()` seeding) so a user cannot undo the seed away.
+
+**`MemNoteStore`** — snapshot-based local history so the engine still
+has working undo without a CRDT (tests / non-collaborative use). Undo
+emits a `replace` remote change so the view reflects it, mirroring how
+the Yorkie store's undo comes back through `subscribeRemote`.
+
+**`note-sync.ts`** — wrap the per-`ViewUpdate` `editText` loop in
+`store.batch()`.
+
+**`editor.ts`** — `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })`;
+bind `Mod-z` / `Mod-Shift-z` / `Mod-y` to the store (skipped in
+read-only); `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo` delegate to the
+store. Vim's `u` / `<C-r>` go through `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`,
+which the vim adapter looks up at call time — override them once to
+route to the note store resolved from the view's `noteStoreFacet`, else
+vim undo would silently no-op with CM history disabled.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] `NoteStore`: `batch` / `undo` / `redo` / `canUndo` / `canRedo`
+- [ ] `MemNoteStore`: snapshot history + `replace` emission on undo/redo
+- [ ] `YorkieNoteStore`: ambient root, `withUpdate`, batch, undo floor,
+      `doc.history` delegation
+- [ ] `note-sync.ts`: wrap local edits in `store.batch()`
+- [ ] `editor.ts`: disable CM history, history keymap → store, API
+      delegation, vim command routing
+- [ ] Tests: batch grouping = 1 undo unit, undo floor, peer-edit
+      preservation (churn regression), no-echo on undo, MemNoteStore
+      history, engine-level keybinding
+- [ ] `docs/design/notes/notes.md`: Yorkie-native undo section
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Time-based keystroke coalescing (Yorkie's undo unit is the change;
+  Docs and Slides behave the same way).
+- `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands in vim (the vim package snapshots those
+  handlers at module load, so they cannot be re-routed).
